summary: Active Alberta wildfire lookout, a 30 m steel lattice tower that Alberta's lookout layer dates to 2004; no site-specific history or access source found.

facts.design: Steel tower (Alberta record), lattice observation tower (OpenStreetMap)

access.note: Active Alberta wildfire lookout (record ACTIVE Y, access mode drive). No source read says the public may enter the grounds or climb the tower.

facts.agency: Alberta Wildfire, within Agriculture and Forestry

events.note: Alberta wildfire lookout layer gives 2004 as the year constructed.

evidence.supports: 127 wildfire lookout sites across the boreal forest and Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: 127 wildfire lookout sites are located throughout Alberta's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: sites isolated; staff must be prepared
evidence.quote: Wildfire lookout sites are isolated and the staff that work them must be prepared for a wide range of possibilities
including an encounter with a curious bear

corrections.why: The Alberta record marks the lookout active (ACTIVE Y). No source read says it is closed, and none says the public may enter it.

sources.title: Alberta wildfire lookout layer (friaa_firesmart_vector_data), attribute query for three sites

notes_for_editor: Thin on history and staffing: the only site-specific sources are the Alberta lookout layer and OpenStreetMap. The brief's 'closed' access is not supported by any source read. The Huckleberry Fire Lookout in Glacier National Park, Montana, is a different tower and must not be mixed in.
